title: Capacity-aware SLO relaxation with regional soft-eviction safeguard
author: Sofia Ramirez
release_notes: Adds a capacity-aware temporary SLO relaxation policy and a regional soft-eviction safeguard to avoid noisy mass-evictions during transient capacity pressure. No user-visible API changes; operational knob under feature flag.
description: Context: We saw repeated cascade evictions during multi-region capacity spikes where strict SLO enforcement triggered aggressive circuit breakers, causing higher tail latency and customer throttles (SUP-9812). This PR introduces a capacity-aware, timebound SLO relaxation layer plus a regional soft-eviction safeguard that stages evictions to avoid synchronized mass-drains. What changed: 1) control/allocator: add 'capacity-aware slo_relaxation' policy that dynamically relaxes non-critical SLOs by a configurable percentage when sustained node-utilization exceeds a threshold for a hold window; 2) routing/eviction: introduce 'soft-eviction' state where instances are marked for probabilistic eviction over a decay window instead of immediate hard drain, enabling load to bleed off while respecting per-tenant priority buckets; 3) telemetry: new metrics (slo_relaxation.active, soft_eviction.pending, soft_eviction.success_rate) and traces for decision points; 4) ops: feature flag rts.slo_relaxation_v1 and runtime knobs for threshold/decay; 5) tests: end-to-end canary harness and unit coverage for decision logic. Motivation: allow graceful degradation that is both capacity- and cost-aware: we prefer slight SLO slack for low-priority requests over wholesale region failovers or bulk evictions which amplify disruption. Implementation notes: the relaxation algorithm is conservative by default (5% token latency budget increase, 2-minute hold window) and respects tenant-priority masks; the soft-eviction uses jittered timers and a token-bucket backoff to limit eviction rate per-region. Operation guidance: defaults are safe for most clusters; ops can tune threshold and relaxation_pct per-capacity class. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal design doc: https://linear.app/ENG/1428/capacity-aware-slo-relaxation) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration canary in perf-lab - [x] metrics + dashboard patches - [x] feature-flag gating - [x] rollout playbook attached (see PR artifacts) Commits: 3 commits (initial implementation, metrics + tests, docs + rollback hooks). High-level changed files: control/allocator/policy_manager.go, control/allocator/slo_relaxation.go, routing/eviction/soft_eviction.go, routing/eviction/soft_eviction_test.go, telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml, ops/feature_flags.yaml, docs/ops/slo-relaxation.md, examples/perf-canary/config.yml. Review conversation summary: Marcus Lin: "Can we make tenant-priority mask evaluation O(1) to avoid runtime cost?" — Author: "Updated mask cache to constant-time lookup and added microbenchmark (see commit 2)." Aisha Patel: "How do we avoid oscillation between relaxed and strict states under flapping load?" — Author: "Added hold window and exponential backoff on relaxation decay; documented rationale and added unit tests for flapping scenario." Ethan Zhao: "Suggest lowering default relaxation_pct to 3% for small regions." — Author: "Left default at 5% but exposed knob and wrote guidance; lowered default for regions with <8 GPUs in ops playbook." CI history: Initial run failed lint due to unused import in soft_eviction_test.go; fixed in commit 3. Integration perf canary showed reduced peak eviction rate in staging (40% -> 7%) with 1.8% median latency increase on low-priority traffic. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in staging for 24h, enable in one EU region with canary traffic split 5%, monitor slo_relaxation.active, soft_eviction.success_rate, region_eviction_rate and rollback in 30m if region_eviction_rate increases. Merge: squashed and merged after approvals from all reviewers and green CI. Post-merge actions: deploy to dedicated canary clusters, coordinate on-call rotation for first 48h, add alert thresholds to SLO dashboard. Notes: This is an operationally-sensitive change; although not a breaking API change, treat rollout as a minor incident risk and follow ops playbook.
